newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares recover from slip on Yeltsin health.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares recover from slip on Yeltsin health.

text.p: Russian shares recovered losses after a midday dip on news that President Boris Yeltsin would remain in hospital all week.
Operators said significant Western demand kept share prices firm, but that Thursday trade would probably not see the nervous market move significantly.
The Russian Trading System index ticked up 0.18 percent to 243.46 on overall market volume of $34 million.
Mosenergo closed up at $1.33 after dropping to $1.29, the level at Tuesday's closing, on the Yeltsin news. LUKoil finished at $13.10, still off from $13.50 earlier but up from $12.85 on Tuesday.
"The market is firmly standing at its new level," said Regent European Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov.
A share rally which began over Christmas slowed early in the week in what traders said was a breather that would not brake the market's overall upward trend.
"There is a correction, but it is small. Some paper simply won't fall -- there is a lot of money in the market," said Creditanstalt-Grant senior trader Andrei Galperin.
The chief Kremlin doctor said Yeltsin would be in the hospital all week because of risks of complications to pneumonia, for which he was sent to hospital last week.
Both operators said the market would likely begin climbing by week's end, though Galperin said Thursday would be flat.
